column1: # OUTSIDE_ARIZONA_BASELINE.tsv -- arizona_tests: what the ONE ICON ORACLE answers only from INSIDE ITS OWN
# IMPLEMENTATION, named beside the package so the graded denominator is the set a second implementation of
# the Icon LANGUAGE could ever reach.  ceo CEO-527 (2026-09-10), on the cfo's measurement; written and
# re-measured by hq_T 2026-09-10 under CEO-532.  Format and reader are the sister package's
# (jcon_tests/OUTSIDE_ARIZONA_BASELINE.tsv, hq_P) -- ONE shape, never a second one.
# FORMAT: name<TAB>CLASS<TAB>reason.  ⛔ NAME IS THE PACKAGE-RELATIVE PATH WITHOUT THE EXTENSION
# (`general/cfuncs`), never a bare basename: this package ships TWO subdirectories and UNGRADABLE.tsv's own
# header already rules a bare name ambiguous here.  That is the ONE divergence from the jcon file, which is
# flat and keys by basename; the reader in test_icon_arizona_suite.sh matches the runner's own `$sub/$name`
# identity, so the key and the census agree by construction rather than by convention.
# ⛔⭐⭐ WHY THESE TWO ROWS ARE NOT THE USUAL SHAPE, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THE FILE.  Every other OUTSIDE row
# in this repo says THE ORACLE CANNOT ANSWER (it refuses to compile, or never terminates).  Arizona icont
# answers both of these perfectly -- and that is exactly the problem, because it answers them out of a C
# shared library that ships in ITS OWN bin and out of ITS OWN runtime descriptor layout.  ⭐ THE GROUND TRUTH
# FOR THESE TWO .std FILES IS NOT THE ICON LANGUAGE; IT IS THE CONTENTS OF ONE IMPLEMENTATION'S libcfunc.so.
# A ref like that cannot be matched by implementing Icon, only by embedding iconx, so it grades the wrong
# thing forever -- the SELF-PIN/ORACLE-DIFF distinction one level further out: an oracle-cut ref is still
# only as portable as the thing the oracle reached for to produce it.
# THE MEASUREMENT, taken 2026-09-10 by hq_T at SCRIP 2bdee91cc, corpus 9e9319641 (every number here is one
# command a reader can repeat):
#   1. THE TWO FEATURE WORDS.  `every write(&features)` under /home/resources/icon-master/bin/icont prints
#      ten lines including `dynamic loading` and `external values`; the same program under ./scrip --run
#      prints eight -- the SAME LIST MINUS THOSE TWO WORDS, and nothing else differs.  So the divergence is
#      not incidental to these programs: the oracle DECLARES the two capabilities they are named for, and we
#      DECLARE that we do not have them.  &features is the language's own way of saying this, and it is
#      already answering the question correctly on both sides.
#   2. WHAT CURING WOULD MEAN, and it is why nobody owes work here.  `nm -D --undefined-only
#      /home/resources/icon-master/bin/libcfunc.so` leaves 15 symbols unresolved, of which NINE are iconx's
#      own runtime: alcexternal alcfile alcreal alcstr cnv_c_str cnv_int cnv_real cnv_str getdbl (plus
#      nulldesc, palnum, rgbkey).  iconx resolves them at dlopen time from itself.  For SCRIP to run these
#      two programs it would have to dlopen ANOTHER IMPLEMENTATION'S library and stand behind ITS allocator,
#      ITS converters and ITS `struct descrip` layout -- embedding iconx's runtime, not implementing Icon.
#      ⭐ The `external` type in extlvals.std is the same fact wearing its user-visible face: `external_1(0)`,
#      `xstr_3(00324:bite)` and `xreal_7(111.1)` are images of C structs allocated by that library.
#   3. WHAT WE PRINT TODAY, which is the honest answer and not a defect: both programs die on line 1 with
#      `cannot find "libcfunc.so" on path ". ."` -- our pathload looked, said so, and stopped.  m3 rc=1 for
#      both.  ⛔ AND FINDING THE FILE WOULD NOT HELP: it is on this box, at the path in (2), and loading it
#      is step (2)'s problem, not a search-path fix.  A reader who cures only the diagnostic will believe
#      they are one FPATH away from green.
#   4. THE COST OF THE EXCLUSION, stated so it can be checked rather than trusted: 61 differing lines leave
#      the board, cfuncs 20 and extlvals 41, MEASURED per program against its own .std, not apportioned from
#      a total.  Two programs leave the graded denominator; the PASS counts do not move.
# ⛔ MIRRORED INTO THE LOCKDOWN BUCKETS, which is what keeps the population summing: both rows also sit in
# UNGRADABLE.tsv as ORACLE_CONTRACT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED with the SAME reason -- a ruling, nobody owes work.  ONE
# PROGRAM CARRIES ONE RULING and the two files may never disagree about WHY (jcon's tpp paid for that once).
# The class is the closed vocabulary's (lib_inventory.sh), and it is the right member by that file's own
# admission test -- COULD THIS RULING BE OVERTURNED FOR THE WHOLE CLASS AT ONCE? -- because one decision
# about dynamic loading moves both programs together, and any third that links cfunc with it.
# ⭐ THE PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN THIS PACKAGE AND IT IS THE SAME TWO WORDS: general/features.icn was ruled
# ORACLE_CONTRACT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED long before CEO-527, because its output "enumerates the ORACLE build
# (co-expressions, dynamic loading, external values, ...) [and] a different implementation legitimately prints
# a different set, so diffing it would grade the BUILD, not the language."  cfuncs and extlvals are that exact
# ruling applied to the programs that USE the two features instead of the one that PRINTS them -- so this is
# not a new principle admitted for two reds; it is an existing ruling reaching the rest of its own class.
# ⛔ Note upstream's own harness agrees about features.icn (Test-icon runs it as a banner and never diffs it)
# and does NOT agree about these two: upstream diffs them, because for upstream the build IS the oracle.
# That asymmetry is the whole content of the ruling and is why it had to be made rather than inherited.
# ⛔⭐⭐ THE OBJECTION THIS FILE HAS TO ANSWER, WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN LEFT FOR THE NEXT READER TO RAISE.
# lib_inventory.sh carries an arm whose whole purpose is to stop exactly this direction of motion, and its
# wording points straight at these two rows: "If the oracle grades it and we do not, it is GRADED and RED."
# It was earned -- hq_C measured 240 prolog exclusions, every one individually honest, composing into a
# denominator that could not fall.  ⭐ THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT SEPARATES THESE ROWS FROM THAT CASE IS NOT
# "the reason is better written": it is that THE RULING WOULD STAND UNCHANGED IF SCRIP WERE PERFECT AT
# EVERYTHING ELSE.  No amount of implementing the Icon LANGUAGE reaches these two .std files, because what
# they encode is one implementation's C library and one implementation's descriptor layout -- so the red
# they contribute can never fall by the work this project exists to do, and a denominator that includes
# them is measuring something nobody is building.  The 240-row case fails that test exactly: every one of
# those would have gone green the day the compiler improved.
# ⛔ APPLY THE TEST, NOT THE PRECEDENT.  A future row here that would go green if we simply got better at
# Icon belongs in the graded denominator, red, with an owner -- however well its reason reads.
# ⛔ THE STALENESS ARM IS NOT icont -s -c HERE, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS.  Re-proving that the ORACLE still
# refuses is the jcon file's check and it is vacuous for this class: the oracle never refused.  The fact that
# can change is OURS -- so the runner re-reads SCRIP's OWN &features every run and REFUSES the exclusion the
# day both words appear in it.  An exclusion list that can only ever lower a number is not a correction; this
# one can raise it, automatically, on the first run after the capability lands.
# ⚠ NAMED, NOT OWED: general/ALL.icn (our generated container, graded by no runner today) carries both
# programs as entries 7 and 24 of ALL.csv.  Nothing reads that container's refs at present, so no board
# double-counts these two -- but whoever wires it must apply this file there too, or the exclusion holds in
# one instrument and not the other.
general/cfuncs
column3: DYNAMIC LOADING -- the feature word is icont's own: `&features` under /home/resources/icon-master/bin/icont lists `dynamic loading`, ours does not (measured 2026-09-10, ten lines vs eight, that word and `external values` the only difference). The program is `link cfunc` plus 18 lines of calls; ipl/cfuncs/cfunc.icn is a stub file whose every procedure is `return(NAME:=pathload("libcfunc.so","NAME"))!a`, so its whole content is dynamic loading and its .std (bitcount/vword/lgconv/unpack/pack) is the output of C in iconx's bin. ⛔ NOT AN ORACLE REFUSAL and NOT OUR VENDORING: icont compiles and runs it clean and its .std was re-cut from the live oracle 2026-09-09 (UNGRADABLE.tsv's whole-suite re-read, 90/90 agree). CURING IT MEANS EMBEDDING iconx: nm -D on that libcfunc.so leaves alcexternal alcfile alcreal alcstr cnv_c_str cnv_int cnv_real cnv_str getdbl undefined, resolved from iconx itself at dlopen. We print `cannot find "libcfunc.so" on path ". ."`, rc=1, 20 differing lines. ceo CEO-527.

column3: EXTERNAL VALUES -- the second feature word, same source and same measurement: icont's `&features` lists `external values`, ours does not. Same `link cfunc` dependency as general/cfuncs (extxmin, extxstr, extxreal are pathload stubs in the same file), and one step worse for a second implementation: the .std does not merely need the library's ANSWERS, it pins the IMAGES of C structs that library allocates -- `external: external_1(0)`, `xstr: xstr_3(00324:bite)`, `xreal: xreal_7(111.1)`, their `===` identity, and their position under `sort()` among a record. That is iconx's `struct descrip` layout and its external-block numbering as ground truth, which no implementation of the Icon language can reproduce except by adopting it. We print `cannot find "libcfunc.so" on path ". ."`, rc=1, 41 differing lines. ceo CEO-527.
